newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares close up on expanded turnover.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares close up on expanded turnover.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index maintained its upward trend and closed slightly higher, boosted by a steady advance in the A share market, brokers said.
The B share index edged up 0.63 points or 0.43 percent to end at 148.86 points, with turnover swelling to HK$107.09 million from Wednesday's HK$95 million.
The A share index rose 6.52 points or 1.83 percent to finish at 362.4 points as turnover expanded to 8.05 billion yuan from 6.77 billion yuan in the previous session.
Brokers said the B share market was supported by bullish sentiment in the A share market, fuelled in part by a strong performance from leader Shenzhen Development Bank.
The banking issue climbed 0.65 yuan to 18.14 yuan on heavy volume of 26.48 million shares. Brokers said they expected the bank to show good 1996 results and attractive dividends.
Shenzhen-based China Nonferrous Holdings Ltd, which listed 18 million A shares and two million staff shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, closed the session at 19.50 yuan.
The A shares were issued at 8.00 yuan each earlier this month and the staff shares were offered at 2.00 yuan each in 1993.
Retailer Foshan Xinghua Group Co Ltd, which listed 16 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, ended its debut at 15.99 yuan versus a recent offer price of 6.74 yuan per share.

Large-cap newcomer Shantui, a bulldozer manufacturer, was the worst performer and retreated 0.38 yuan or 4.1 percent to 8.88 yuan, after 36.53 million shares were traded on profit-taking, brokers said.
On the B share market, Shenbao, the sharpest gainer, surged HK$0.43 or 8.74 percent to HK$5.35 on volume of 399,220 shares on speculative buying.
Brokers said Shenbao's plan to move its plant to the suburbs of Shenzhen from the city's centre and convert its current address to a commercial complex was likely to boost earnings.
Conglomerate Zhonghao rode the trend to rise HK$0.19 or 4.65 percent to HK$4.28 on thin trade of 177,520 shares.
Property developer Hainan Pearl River firmed HK$0.14 to HK$3.24 on the session's most active trade of 2.29 million shares.

Brokers said the advance was spurred by market talk that the company would post healthier results for the second half of 1996, compared with the first half, on sale of a real estate project in Shanghai.
China Marine Container was the biggest loser on profit-taking and slid HK$0.19 or 2.09 percent to HK$8.88.
